title: My philosophy regarding abs training
summary: NH explains that the core is key to an aesthetic physique, especially for someone with a thick waist like him. He trains abs daily, mainly by supersetting 60-100 leg or knee raises with pull-ups, plus occasional end-of-session isolation. His upper abs are well developed from years of full-range weighted crunches (sometimes an hour at a time) starting at 14, so they show even at higher body fat, while his lower abs lag because he never did leg raises back then.

claims.claim: Abs are key in bodybuilding; the core brings the physique together, enhancing the look if strong and making everything look worse if weak.
He started lifting at 14 and was obsessed with getting a six-pack, overdoing ab work, which now benefits him.
He trains abs every day, supersetting all chin-ups and pull-ups with leg or knee raises, totaling about 60-100 leg raise reps daily.
Leg raises focus on the lower abs, the area he most wants to develop.
In his youth he did full-range crunches with feet anchored under furniture, progressing from bodyweight to dumbbells and plates, sometimes for an hour while watching TV.
On his first real gym visit, a friend's trainer claimed training a muscle more than 10 minutes was a waste, which he calls bro science; he wanted at least 30 minutes of abs.
Crunches built his upper four abs very well, but since he never did leg raises his lower abs lag.
Today he gets most core stimulation from compound movements plus supersetted ab work rather than hour-long sessions.
Having heavily trained abs in the past, they bulge and show through even at fairly high body fat; similarly his heavily trained biceps keep growing with minimal work.
End-of-workout ab finishers when needed: leg raises with a dumbbell between the feet, side leg raises, banded crunches; he rarely does crunches now and prioritizes floor leg raises for lower abs.
With a small waist you can get away with less ab size and definition, but with a thick waist like his you need big abs so eyes read 'strong waist' instead of 'wide waist', an illusion strategy.
His ab training is nothing fancy: the same movements repeated every day, which is what bodybuilding is.
